ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To look around is to turn and look at a person, direction, or assembly.
EvidenceBody: The verb retains that visual sense in Emperor Suzong's complaint that Nanyang Huizhong does not look at him and in an unnamed monk's looking east and west for the absent Changqing Da'an. Chan records also make it a recurrent teaching-seat stage direction. At an opening of the hall Xuedou Chongxian “looked around at the assembly” (顧視大眾) before speaking; Yungai Zhiyong follows the look with a shout and questions concerning host and guest. In one encounter Mazu Daoyi merely looks, Yangshan Huiji comments on the look, and the exchange ends. Ciji Cong compresses speech and action still further: “then he looked around at the assembly and said, ‘stop!’” (乃顧視大眾曰休). Yulin Tongxiu looks left and right, strikes the staff, and leaves the seat (顧視左右，卓拄杖，下座). Thus an ordinary look is bent into an observable public-address action of the teaching seat; the entry does not assign the look an unspoken symbolic message.
